categories.main_business_segments: PARK24 operates three main business segments: Domestic Parking Business, Overseas Parking Business, and Mobility Business. The Domestic and Overseas Parking segments focus on the operation and management of hourly and monthly parking lots, while the Mobility segment provides car sharing, rental car services, and related mobility solutions such as road assistance.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary parking management systems, including the TONIC online management platform and Times Tower payment machines, as well as license plate recognition cameras for next-generation parking services. Digitalization and integration of smartphone applications are central to service delivery, and the company is advancing EV charging infrastructure and data-driven operational optimization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include individual drivers, corporate clients, and facility owners seeking parking management solutions. The end markets are urban and suburban areas with high parking demand, as well as users of car sharing and rental services, both in Japan and internationally.
categories.geographic_coverage: PARK24 has a strong presence in Japan and operates internationally in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia, and Taiwan. The domestic market remains the largest, but overseas operations, particularly in the UK and Australia, are significant contributors.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily at the downstream end of the mobility and parking value chain, directly providing services to end users and facility owners. It also acts as a platform operator, integrating upstream suppliers (equipment, vehicles) and downstream customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding and integrating four networks—people (members), vehicles (mobility), destinations (cities), and parking lots—while promoting digital transformation, sustainability, and service innovation. R&D is focused on digital platforms, EV infrastructure, and enhancing user convenience through technology and data utilization.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated mainly from parking fees (hourly and monthly), car sharing and rental fees, and ancillary services such as road assistance and payment solutions. The company also earns management fees from facility owners and leverages a membership-based model for mobility services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In Japan, PARK24 is the market leader in parking and car sharing services, with a dominant share in both segments. Overseas, it competes with local and global parking operators. The company positions itself as a global mobility service platform aiming for world No.1 in both profitability and service quality.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending October 2024, consolidated sales reached 370.9 billion yen (+12.4% YoY), with operating profit of 38.7 billion yen (+21.0% YoY) and net profit attributable to parent of 18.6 billion yen (+6.2% YoY). The company has demonstrated strong post-pandemic recovery and targets further growth, aiming for 474 billion yen in sales and 44.5 billion yen in operating profit by FY2027.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: PARK24 differentiates itself through its extensive, integrated parking and mobility networks, advanced digital platforms, and a focus on user convenience and seamless service. Its ability to offer both parking and mobility solutions, combined with data-driven management and a commitment to sustainability (e.g., EV charging), provides unique value to customers and partners.
